research_question: How accurately does frozen ReproCheck v0.7 extract unseen metric table cells across classification, segmentation, speech, and translation repositories?

selection.ranking: ascending SHA-256 of repository_id + NUL + repository-relative path
selection.sampling: include declared always_include files, then first N matching files by registered hash ranking

annotation_scope.include: cells with exactly one finite numeric value under an unambiguous registered metric header
exclude: cells containing zero or multiple numeric values
training parameters, speed, memory, FLOPs, and model size
derived interpretation not explicit in the table
annotation_scope.normalization: explicit percentages and unit-interval metric values above 1 are divided by 100; BLEU, WER, CER, RMSE, MAE, and R2 preserve their reported numeric scale unless explicitly percent
annotation_scope.annotation_independence: annotation code must not import reprocheck or inspect evaluator output
annotation_scope.review: all unique accepted headers and all ambiguous rejected headers reviewed internally before evaluator run

evaluation.matching: multiset equality by canonical metric and numeric value
evaluation.uncertainty: Wilson 95% intervals for precision and recall

decision_policy.parser_changes_after_primary_output: require version 0.8 or later and a new unseen holdout
decision_policy.annotation_corrections_after_primary_out: record separately and never replace primary metrics

known_limitations: Repositories and metric families were selected by the project author, not an external evaluator.
Annotations will have one internal reviewer and no blinded adjudication unless external reviewers are added.
The corpus remains public-documentation data and does not test OCR or private reports.
The fairseq repository is archived, but its pinned artifacts remain valid public evidence.
